subject: botany_2
question_text: Write a note on agricultural and horticultural applications of auxins.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.26, printed question 20. insider_note: This question is a LIST, and the marks are in the number of distinct uses. Six named uses beats two well-explained ones here.

steps.label: What auxins are
steps.margin_note: Source, the two natural ones, the two synthetic ones. Five lines.
lines: Auxins are plant growth hormones produced at
the STEM TIPS and ROOT TIPS.
Natural auxins isolated from plants are
indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and indole butyric
acid (IBA). NAA and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins.
steps.why: Auxins are made at the growing tips and move down, which is why almost every use below is about a tip, a cutting, or the buds a tip controls.
common_mistakes: Saying auxins are made in the leaves. They are made at the STEM and ROOT TIPS.
Naming no example. IAA, IBA, NAA and 2,4-D are the four worth writing.
steps.memory_tip: Made at the tips, and every use follows from that.

steps.label: Rooting and fruit growth
steps.margin_note: Four numbered uses. Keep the numbering running across all three steps.
lines: 1. Auxins start ROOT formation in stem cuttings.
This is widely used in horticulture to propagate
plants from cuttings.
2. Auxins promote fruit growth, for example in
tomatoes.
3. Auxins prevent PREMATURE FRUIT DROP.
4. Auxins control xylem differentiation and help
in growth.
steps.why: A cutting has no roots and no root tip, so supplying auxin from outside does the job the missing tip would have done.
common_mistakes: Saying auxins prevent fruit growth. They PROMOTE it.
Leaving out the cutting. Rooting a cutting is the main horticultural use.
steps.memory_tip: A cutting has no tip, so the auxin is supplied by hand.

steps.label: Weed control and lawns
steps.margin_note: Say which group is killed and which is spared. That contrast is the mark.
lines: 5. The synthetic auxin 2,4-D kills DICOT weeds
but does not affect mature MONOCOTS.
6. So 2,4-D is used to prepare and maintain
lawns, where the grass is a monocot and the
weeds are dicots.
steps.why: A grass lawn is monocot and its weeds are dicots, so a weedkiller that only harms dicots clears the lawn without harming it.
common_mistakes: Saying 2,4-D kills all plants. It kills DICOT weeds and spares mature monocots.
Leaving out the lawn. It is the named horticultural application.
steps.memory_tip: Grass is a monocot, so a dicot killer leaves the lawn standing.

steps.label: Apical dominance in practice
steps.margin_note: Name apical dominance, then the two applications. This is the last mark.

lines.text: Remove the tip and the side buds grow

lines: 7. The shoot tip produces auxin that suppresses
the growth of lateral buds. This is APICAL
DOMINANCE.
8. Removing the shoot tip removes that
suppression, so the lateral buds grow.
9. This is applied in TEA plantations and in
hedge-making, to get bushy growth.
steps.why: Cutting the tip removes the source of the auxin, so the buds below are released and the plant spreads sideways instead of upward.
common_mistakes: Saying removing the tip stops growth. It REDIRECTS growth into the lateral buds.
Naming no application. Tea plantations and hedges are the named ones.
steps.memory_tip: Cut the top and the plant grows outward instead of upward.
